title: Learning double-over-the-top in stocking feet and becoming master of the club
summary: In California he practiced day and night, cried on getting the step at dawn, and the one step made him the talk of the Hoofers Club.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: However, I go into California on the Fantages circuit I think it was at that time in the year of 1921 and since they wrote me out of this Comedy Club or Hoofers Club, whatever you want to call it, I went to California and thought I'd learn dancing while I was away. So I did. I studied it while I was away, day and night. When I came back I stayed up all night to learn the one step. I was dancing until about 6 o'clock in the morning. And the restaurant was open, I got through with the step. I had to cry because I was so overjoyed that I had gotten the step that I wanted called "double-over-the-top"and I go around to this restaurant at 41st and 8th Avenue to get some coffee and donuts after I
finished, this was in the morning. I had to take my shoes off at night to keep the sound from going through the floor, you know, to learn this dancing, the step, you know?
Why did you take your shoes off?

Because I made too much noise tapping with shoes on, too much noise. If you are downstairs and I'm upstairs and I was dancing over you, what happens? Then if you're next door what happens at 3 o'clock in the morning, 4 o'clock in the morning, what happens then? Just like that dog over there, that's in the daytime, too. What are you going to do at 4 o'clock in the morning with a sound going out like that.

So that's what I did, took my shoes off and danced stocking feet until I got the step, and I got it and I got so happy about it I cried and I went down to the corner to get some coffee and stuff and went back up to Harlem the next day to see what they had against

me this time. So everybody would dance, dance -- come around to be time for me I could go out and dance, so I danced, and I did this step, that was it. That one step stopped everything, the one I stayed up all night for, that made me the master of the dancing at the club, for the Hoofers Club. Everybody talked about me then. "You ought to see that step. You ought to see so-and-so and so."
So I got the dancing down and I wanted to do some other kind of thing, I wanted to mix my style up, do negro dancing and white dancing together.
